rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source-verification maintainer block required, each source carries a freshness stamp (incl. §11a due-date discipline)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Source line 107: `[checked:2026-07-30 result:OK due:2027-01-30]` for the designing-agentic-loops URL. 2026-07-30 + 6 months = 2027-01-30 exactly — this is the `checked+6mo` arithmetic §11a explicitly bans ('Never `checked`+6mo — ... the arithmetic grants a three-weeks-from-stale source a fresh year'). Harm the rule prevents: silently re-extending an already-stale source's apparent freshness window at re-check time rather than anchoring to publication date. Harm is only partly mitigated here — the maintainer block is transparent that the source sits outside the normal 6-month window 'by decision' (so a reader isn't deceived about currency), but the specific due-date VALUE was computed via the banned method rather than an honest anchor (e.g. `due:none` matching the adjacent lethal-trifecta stamp's delegated/durable treatment, or `due:asap`), so the automated `source-freshness.sh` re-audit trigger is set by the wrong clock.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recompute due: either `due:none` with the same 'maintainer decision, dated in body' reasoning already given (matching the Cherny/lethal-trifecta precedent), or an honestly-anchored date, not checked-date+6mo.
